note: A release log for BMTRE (the Trakt recommendation engine) — every real scoring/data-pipeline change, with a real before-and-after of the engine wherever one exists. Entries from Session 53 onward carry real leave-one-out eval.js numbers (computeEvalMetrics(): precision@10/25/50/100, MAE); entries before Session 53 predate that harness (it didn't exist yet) and carry a qualitative before/after instead, quoted from the same real verification each session actually ran. Populated by mining CLAUDE.md's own session log for every entry with a real, verifiable before/after claim — not reconstructed from memory. New entries are appended going forward as real changes ship; this file is never used for scoring, purely a human-readable history.

entries.title: BMTRE Phase 1 launches — rule-based scorer ported from BBRE
entries.summary: First working engine.js: titleKey(type,tmdbId)-based indexing (no fuzzy title matching needed at all, unlike the book engine's history), buildIndexes()/genreBonus()/forward-reverse similarToIds matching/confidenceScore()/reason() ported directly from the book engine's shapes. No eval harness existed yet — scoring correctness verified via a synthetic-data smoke test (hand-traced one result's score component-by-component), not a real precision measurement.

before.note: No recommendation engine for movies/TV existed at all.

after.note: All 28 real watchlist titles score and rank correctly, though every title shows an honest "not enough data yet" reason pending TMDB enrichment (enrichedMetadata.json still empty at this point).

entries.title: matchPointScale() — corrects for Bill's ~2x more loved shows than loved movies
entries.summary: The forward/reverse similar-title signal could only ever compare a candidate against loved titles of its own type, and movies structurally had far fewer loved anchors (50) than shows (99), capping every movie's ceiling. matchPointScale(type, lovedCountByType) scales the smaller pool's per-match point value up by the measured ratio, self-correcting as the pools shift.

before.note: Gladiator (a real director match + 2 forward + 1 reverse title match) capped at 85.9/100; only 1 of 116 movies scored ≥63.

after.note: Gladiator scores 99.8/100; movies scoring ≥63 rose from 1 to 11 of 116. Median barely moved (41.9→42.0) since the fix raises the ceiling for a strong match, not the typical case — correctly.

entries.title: normalizeGenre() — merges TMDB's separate movie/show genre vocabularies
entries.summary: TMDB labels the same concept differently by type (movie "Action" vs. show "Action & Adventure"), silently splitting lovedGenres credit into two smaller buckets instead of one combined one.

before.note: A loved movie's "Action" (15 uses) and a loved show's "Action & Adventure" (7 uses) accumulated into separate lovedGenres buckets instead of a combined 22.

after.note: Genre credit combines correctly across types via GENRE_ALIASES — verified via diagnostic not to be the main driver of the movie score-ceiling gap (matchPointScale above was), but a real, independent fix.

entries.title: omdbSignal() — audience/critic score and awards wired into live scoring
entries.summary: audienceScore()/awardsScore() had been display-only since Session 49, pending real OMDb data. With 890 titles now OMDb-enriched, folded into baseSignals(): audience/critic neutral point set to 80 (this dataset's real measured median), capped ±6; awards scaled to a max +4 bonus so "won something" doesn't read the same as "won everything."

before.note: audienceScore()/awardsScore() computed and cached but never affected a candidate's rank.

after.note: 89 of 227 live candidates moved score, deltas bounded exactly as designed (max +10, max -6), zero candidates hit the 100 clamp. The Death of Stalin (91 audience score + real awards) gained the most (+6.3); Southpaw/Big George Foreman each lost the full -6, a fair correction now backed by real audience data.

entries.title: discover_candidates.js ranks and caps movies and shows separately
entries.summary: Root cause of the "top movie score stuck at 71" complaint: discovery ranked movies and shows together in one combined citation-count list, and since Bill loves ~2x more shows, shows structurally dominated the pool before scoring ever got a chance to differentiate a movie.

before.note: Real candidate pool: 106 movies vs. 221 shows despite 1,575 untapped movie candidates sitting in the citation reservoir; top movie score 71.

after.note: Pool rebalanced to a clean 100 movies / 100 shows after a real re-discovery + re-enrichment + prune; top movie score rose to Deadpool & Wolverine at 82.7, with 4 movies over 80 and 14 over the old 71 ceiling (Raging Bull, Saving Private Ryan, Full Metal Jacket among them).

entries.title: recencyBonusMovie()/recencyBonusShow() split from one shared curve
entries.summary: Bill: "strongly favor movies from the last 5-10 years, nothing before 2000." The single recencyBonus(year) was split into a steep movie-only curve (+8 at ≤5yr, down to -15 pre-2000-adjacent) and an unchanged show curve, plus a new hard isPreMillenniumMovie() candidate-exclusion filter (watchlist exempt).

before.note: Recency curve identical for movies and shows; pre-2000 movies could freely surface as candidates.

after.note: 0 pre-2000 movies remain in the pool after a real re-discovery + prune; all of the real top-10 movie candidates are from 2017 or later.

entries.title: prune_candidate_pool.js actually calls its own re-edit/non-English filters
entries.summary: isReEdit()/isNonEnglish() existed but were never called when deciding what counts toward the 100-per-type candidate-pool cap — titles that could never surface as a recommendation still occupied real cap slots.

before.note: 42 stale candidates (pre-2000 classics, non-English titles, one theatrical re-edit) occupying cap slots they could never actually be shown from.

after.note: Purged and refilled via a real re-discovery + enrichment + re-prune: clean 100/100 pool, 0 re-edit/non-English/pre-2000 waste.

entries.title: computeEvalMetrics() — BMTRE's first real evaluation harness
entries.summary: Leave-one-out precision@10/25/50/100 + MAE + bottom-50 catch rate, built directly in engine.js (mirroring the book engine's scripts/eval.js, LIKED_THRESHOLD=8/10) so every future scoring change could be measured against a real number, not just spot-checked.

before.note: Every prior BMTRE scoring change (Sessions 44-52) was validated only by inspecting individual candidates by hand — no aggregate accuracy measurement existed for this engine.

after.note: First real measured baseline: BMTRE Accuracy Score 65/100. Every scoring change from this point on in the log below carries real before/after eval.js numbers.

entries.title: castBonus() — top-billed cast affinity signal
entries.summary: topCast (93.4% populated) had been cached but never scored. New idx.lovedActors index plus a small, tiered, capped-at-8 bonus (deliberately smaller than the creator/franchise bonuses, since an actor is less determinative of a title's identity than its director). One of the larger single-change improvements measured for this engine.

before.note: p25/p50 held steady, exact values not individually logged that session

entries.title: franchiseBonus() — TMDB collection/franchise match signal
entries.summary: belongsToCollection was cached on 146 movie titles but never scored, despite 17 of Bill's real loved titles demonstrably following a franchise (Creed I+II, Deadpool 1+2, Sicario 1+2, both Anchorman films).

entries.title: keywordBonus() — TMDB free-form keyword signal, cap tuned against eval.js
entries.summary: TMDB's free-form keywords, previously read only by the isReEdit() filter, are BMTRE's closest analog to the book engine's theme vocabulary. Cap size tuned by sweeping against eval.js, not guessed.

before.note: an initial cap of 4 improved MAE to 18.55 but dropped precision@10 90%→80% — a real regression on the metric this project forbids trading away; reverted.

after.note: cap halved to 2 — held precision@10/25/50/100 exactly unchanged while still improving MAE.

entries.title: subgenreBonus() + toneSignal() — first taxonomy-based scoring signals
entries.summary: New inferSubgenres()/inferTones() deterministic keyword classifiers (21 subgenres, 14 tones at the time) wired into scoring for the first time. subgenreBonus()'s cap swept down to 1.5 after a naive port (scaled straight from genreBonus()'s own thresholds) regressed precision@50; toneSignal()'s multiplier swept 1.5-15, plateauing from ~5, kept at 4.

entries.title: TMDB status field ("Returning Series") recency-gap fix — attempted, reverted
entries.summary: Tried to fix the show-recency gap (an old-but-still-airing show scoring as "old" as a finished one) with a flat status-based credit for ~17.8% of all shows. Both a flat +2 and +1 credit measurably hurt eval.js — reverted rather than shipped, documented as a real, now evidence-backed open gap rather than an unexplored idea.

after.note: both tested credits regressed; not shipped

entries.title: parse_awards() bug fix — 252 records corrected from a wrong zero
entries.summary: enrich_omdb.py's parse_awards() only recognized OMDb's combined "N wins & M nominations total" text shape, silently reading every other real format (bare "N win(s) total", no trailing "total", etc.) as zero recognition. Re-parsed all 1,343 already-cached records locally (no new API calls) — the true zero-recognition rate corrected from a bug-inflated 32.2% to a real 15.4%.

before.note: overnight-session baseline

after.note: one real, accepted boundary-title regression: "Presumed Innocent" (21 real total nominations, previously misparsed to 0) edged out "Deadpool 2" by a 0.37-point margin in a tightly-clustered near-100 cluster. Kept the data fix over reverting a confirmed bug for a single-slot swap at the edge of a high-variance n=10 metric — self-resolved later the same session.

entries.title: Subgenre/tone keyword-synonym expansion restores precision@10 as a side effect
entries.summary: 26 new subgenre + 15 new tone real keyword synonyms added to existing tag buckets (each verified at real frequency first, spot-checked for false positives). Coverage: subgenres 64.6%→69.8%, tones 18.1%→25.6% — both signals already live in scoring.

after.note: restored as a side effect of the coverage expansion, resolving the awards-fix regression above without any further tuning

entries.title: Overnight pass — dismissAdjust(), rewatchStrength(), a swept-and-shipped-inert recency signal
entries.summary: Worked all 9 then-open Improvement Opportunities in one unattended overnight pass. dismissAdjust() (creator-dislike/style-dislike penalties, mirroring the book engine's equivalent) and rewatchStrength() (plays-field normalization) both shipped as verified no-ops today — dormant/inert against current real data, ready to contribute the moment real dismissals or rewatches exist. A show-airing-status weighted signal was swept scale 0-50 and failed at every nonzero value (precision@10 dropped to 90% at the first step) — shipped at scale=0 (real, correct, inert) rather than deleted, to narrow what a future attempt should try.

entries.title: Genre/Subgenre taxonomy redesign — single-valued Genre, curated 65-bucket Subgenre
entries.summary: Bill: "I want genre to be fairly high level and sub-genre to be very specific." 5-phase project: new single-valued inferGenre() (17 canonical values, workbook-seeded, +8-ceiling genreBonus() beat +5 on every eval.js metric), a curated ~65-bucket Subgenre vocabulary (6 genre-duplicative buckets retired, ~40 added from a hand-reviewed workbook), subgenreBonus() thresholds re-swept 18/10/4/1→13/7/3/1 for the denser vocabulary.

before.note: TMDB's raw genres field had Drama on 75.3% of titles (too blunt to discriminate); inferSubgenres() had drifted into doing genre's job too (42.4% of its tag instances were genre-level concepts like historical/war/political sitting flat in the wrong field).

after.note: precision@10/25/50/100 held or improved on every real change across all 5 phases, never traded for a better MAE. No Subgenre bucket exceeds the project's 15%-concentration cap.

entries.title: descSimilarity.js — TF-IDF plot-description similarity signal ported from the book engine
entries.summary: BMTRE had no plot/description-similarity signal at all, unlike the book engine's real, load-bearing descSimilarity.js. Ported the identical tokenizer/TF-IDF/cosine math, adapted to BMTRE's additive-bonus shape. Cap swept 1→2→3 (each step measurably improved precision@100/MAE with p10/25/50 held, plateauing at 3); k swept 5-20 (15+ traded precision@50 for a better MAE, forbidden — k=10 held).

entries.title: subjectBonus() tiers re-swept after Subjects taxonomy consolidation (636→129 buckets)
entries.summary: Denser canonical Subject buckets pushed real per-book loved-title counts up to a max of 8 (was 1-3 under the old fragmented free-form vocabulary), which the old tiers weren't calibrated for.

before.note: dipped to 90% at the old 8/5/2/1 tiers once the consolidation shipped

after.note: fully recovered at new 6/4/2/1 tiers; every other metric held or improved throughout

entries.title: idx.titleAffinity — every rated title now contributes signal, not just 9-10s
entries.summary: 57.1% of Bill's rated titles (every 7 and 8) fed zero signal to lovedGenres/lovedSubgenres/lovedKeywords/lovedActors/lovedCollections/lovedSubjects/the forward-reverse similar-title match, all hard-gated at myRating>=9, while only creatorRatingWeight used a continuous rating-weight. Generalized that continuous-weight shape to the other six (clamped non-negative, so a 6-or-below rating still contributes exactly 0 — purely additive).

after.note: p100's single-point dip is within noise

entries.title: genreSignal() — first negative-preference signal (horror candidates finally penalized)
entries.summary: Horror candidates scored no differently whether Bill loves or dislikes the genre (real dislike rate 33% vs. a 5.7% baseline). Two real regressions were found and root-caused before shipping, not assumed away: a symmetric ±3 clamp pushed already-near-100 candidates past the 100-point display clamp, displacing better matches (fixed: asymmetric, penalty-only); even asymmetric, penalizing every negative delta however small regressed precision@25 via the same clamp-tie mechanism from the other direction (fixed: a -0.5 deadzone, so only genres rated sizably below Bill's own average — mystery -0.53, biography -0.70, horror -1.47 — ever take a penalty).

entries.title: calibrateScore() — a linear recalibration closing the long-standing MAE-vs-baseline gap
entries.summary: matchScore()'s raw 0-100 output was only ever designed to rank candidates correctly relative to each other, never to land on an absolute scale matching myRating*10 directly — real signal existed (Pearson r=0.35 with actual rating) but MAE kept losing to the naive mean-baseline, a caveat repeated across dozens of prior sessions. A simple affine fix: actual ≈ 0.298 × predicted + 55.8, validated via 5-fold cross-validation before shipping (held-out calibrated MAE 10.50 vs. 14.65 uncalibrated vs. 11.03 naive baseline, stable across all 5 folds). Order-preserving by construction and scoped only to the evaluation/accuracy-reporting layer — the live displayed score, ranking, and rec panels are completely untouched.

before.note: raw predicted score's own MAE lost to the naive mean-baseline

after.note: bit-for-bit identical ranking metrics (as designed — this changes only the reported accuracy number, not the live score); calibrated MAE now genuinely beats the naive baseline

entries.title: Dashboard BMTRE Accuracy dial was silently under-measuring signal — a measurement bug, not an engine bug
entries.summary: quality.js's load() called computeEvalMetrics() with only 4 of 6 real parameters, silently defaulting llmTags/reviewedTags to {} even though both were already loaded two lines above (and used correctly by the very next rankAll() call). The dashboard's own "official" accuracy numbers had been diverging from the CLI's for as long as this dial existed.

before.note: Dashboard dial showed precision@10 100.0% vs. the CLI's real 90.0% — an 11-point phantom gap from missing tone/subgenre/reviewed-tag signal in the dial's own computation.

after.note: One-line fix (thread the already-loaded values through); dial now matches the CLI exactly (90/96/98/91) on every subsequent load.

entries.title: discover_explore.py — a second, independent candidate-discovery source
entries.summary: discover_candidates.js sourced every candidate exclusively from loved titles' TMDB similarToIds/recommendedIds — the identical graph baseSignals()'s forward/reverse-match signal (worth up to +24/+12) then rewards a candidate for appearing in. discover_explore.py queries TMDB's genre-filtered /discover endpoint instead, seeded from Bill's real loved-genre mix, never touching the similarity graph — wired into the weekly trakt-discover-candidates.yml workflow.

before.note: 96.0% of the discovered candidate pool came from the exact same graph that then scores it — discovery and scoring were structurally the same question asked twice.

after.note: One deliberately modest real validation run (15 new movies + 15 new shows) dropped the closed-loop share 96.0%→93.8% — the mechanism is proven and keeps chipping away at the share every week the recurring workflow runs.

entries.title: Show-level TMDB popularity — a genuinely unused field finally scored
entries.summary: TMDB's title-level popularity (a trending/buzz metric, distinct from voteCount/voteAverage) had been captured on every enriched title since Session 44 but never read anywhere in scoring. Correlation check found r≈0.002 for movies but a real, monotonic r=0.20 for shows. Weight swept 0-10, then finer 1.5-3.5 — a clean maximum at weight=2.

after.note: verified as a substantively correct swap, not a coin-flip boundary crossing: Breaking Bad (myRating=10) enters the leave-one-out top-10 in place of Presumed Innocent (myRating=7)

entries.title: Season-count and premium-network (HBO/Max) signals — tested twice, both real dead ends
entries.summary: Bill pushed back on the first premium-network negative result with a specific hypothesis ("I tend to love HBO/MAX way more than ABC or NBC, especially recent stuff") — checked directly and found it's genuinely true (premium networks score 2.54 points above Big4 in the 2020+ era specifically). A second, purpose-built recency-interaction signal was swept anyway. Both this and the separate season-count signal were already substantially explained by signals the engine already scores (popularity/vote-count/community-rating/creator-match), so the new credit mostly stacked on titles that already scored well.

before.note: Season count: a real inverted-U pattern (1-2 seasons 7.58 avg → 5-8 seasons 8.61 → 8+ seasons 7.83). Premium network: a real 2.54-point era-bucketed advantage in the 2020s specifically.

after.note: Every tested scale of both signals either changed nothing or only cost precision@50 (98%→94-96%) for no compensating gain. Not shipped; documented as two permanent, evidence-backed dashboard dead-end records.

entries.title: Mutual-citation double-counting fix — correctly diagnosed, but the general-purpose fix regressed broadly
entries.summary: Zack Snyder's Justice League (93.0 raw) had both its forward AND reverse similar-title credit trace to the exact same single mutual TMDB citation with Deadpool, counted as two independent votes instead of one. Checked how widespread this is before building anything: 84% of all forward+reverse matches dataset-wide are mutual citations.

before.note: Zack Snyder's Justice League scoring 93.0 raw, almost entirely off one mutual Deadpool citation counted twice

after.note: the blanket fix correctly dropped Justice League's raw score 91.2→83.6 but regressed the whole pool broadly — most mutual citations are genuine deep corroboration (e.g. The Westies, cited by 5 different loved crime dramas), not artifacts. Not shipped; solved instead via a display-only filter two sessions later.

entries.title: Superhero-subgenre display filter on the You'll Love panel — score untouched
entries.summary: Bill: "exclude comic book movies from the top 10... don't change the score, just filter them out from that one section." The safe, display-only alternative to the scoring fix above, which had already regressed broadly.

after.note: byte-identical, as designed — The Dark Knight/Zack Snyder's Justice League/Doctor Strange are excluded from the You'll Love panel only; they still score and rank normally everywhere else (All Titles table, CSV export, eval.js).

entries.title: prestigeQualityRaw() critic-neutral-point correction (70→80) + badge threshold recalibration
entries.summary: The Prestige score's critic-score term hardcoded an invented neutral point (70) instead of reusing the dataset's own already-validated CRITIC_NEUTRAL (80, already live in real scoring via omdbSignal()). Fixing it would have silently un-badged 86 currently-🏆-badged shows — presented the tradeoff via AskUserQuestion; Bill chose to keep the fix and recalibrate PRESTIGE_BADGE_THRESHOLD to 45 (swept 42-48) to preserve real-world badge coverage.

before.note: Prestige has never been read by matchScore() — a pure display/insight signal

after.note: byte-identical eval.js (display-only fix); the badge population moved from 328 to 346 of 480 real qualifying shows under the recalibrated threshold

entries.title: OMDb enrichment permanent-retry bug — negative-cache marker + 14-day cooldown
entries.summary: A failed OMDb lookup wrote nothing to the cache, so a permanently-failing title (Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story, a real, correctly-sourced IMDb id) was retried every single day forever — and being the sole pending title one day, it alone broke the whole scheduled workflow. Fixed with the same RETRY_COOLDOWN_DAYS pattern the book side already established for the identical failure shape (Session 13d).

before.note: the daily trakt-enrich-omdb.yml workflow was failing outright; engine.js scoring untouched by this pipeline fix

after.note: verified in real production: 530 other pending titles enriched cleanly in the same run, the one real failure got the expected negative-cache marker, OMDb Record Found field reads a genuine 100%/100%

entries.title: diversityRerank() now caps director/creator repetition too, not just genre
entries.summary: diversityRerank()'s only diversity axis was TMDB's raw primary genre, capped per display window — nothing stopped several titles from the same prolific director/showrunner from crowding out a window if franchiseBonus() and a creator match both fired for that person's other work simultaneously. New maxPerCreator option (default 2), reusing the exact defer-not-exclude/backfill-if-thin mechanism the genre cap already uses. Display-only, same as the genre cap — reorders an already-scored list for the rec panels, never touches matchScore()/bmtreScore.

after.note: byte-identical, as designed (display-only fix, computeEvalMetrics() scores one title at a time and never touches diversityRerank()); verified live that today's real top-20 pool for both types stays within the new cap

entries.title: tag_llm.py now asks for subjects too — closes the field-quality-subjects gap at zero extra API cost
entries.summary: inferSubjects() (engine.js) already had the exact right 3-tier shape (reviewed -> keyword -> llmEntry?.subjects), a real live scoring signal (subjectBonus()), but tag_llm.py's prompt never asked the LLM for subjects, so the third tier was permanently empty on the producing side. Added a SUBJECTS canonical-vocabulary constant and wired it into the same already-planned prompt/response, and extended find_llm_tag_gaps.mjs to also select a title purely for a subject gap, not just subgenre/tone. Also fixed a real, separate pre-existing bug found while doing this: the subgenre/tone gap checks never passed inferSubgenres()/inferTones()'s reviewed-tier parameter, wrongly counting a reviewed-workbook-only title as a gap.

before.note: subjects field-quality gap: 228 of ~1,057 titles with no subject at all, 222 with no llmTags.json entry

after.note: verified in real production (run completed, 692-title batch): Subjects population jumped 77.9%→99.2% (1,049 of 1,057 titles), only 18 titles left with any tagging gap at all (12 subgenre, 1 tone, 8 subject) — self-resolved the field-quality-subjects finding

entries.title: Ran genre-explore discovery at real scale (100/type, top 12 loved genres/type), not just a validation batch
entries.summary: The closed-loop-discovery finding measured the independent discover_explore.py source at only a small, deliberately modest validation batch (15 candidates/type) as of Session 59, moving the closed-loop share 96.0%->93.8%. Triggered trakt-discover-candidates.yml for real at genuinely large scale (explore_max_new_per_type=100, explore_top_genres_per_type=12, enrich_batch_size=300) instead of another marginal test. Real GitHub Actions run 34068301783 completed successfully: 71 new genre-explore-sourced candidates added and fully TMDB-enriched (62 movies, 9 shows), candidate pool now 439 titles total (213 movies/226 shows).

before.note: candidate pool closed-loop share (titles cited by a loved title similar/recommended list, matching quality.js's live idx.reverseSimilar computation): 93.8% (Session 59's one small 15/type validation batch)

after.note: closed-loop share dropped to 84.5% (371 of 439 pool titles cited by a loved title) after this real, much larger batch - a 9.3-point real drop vs. the earlier validation batch's 2.2-point move, confirming the mechanism scales rather than being a one-off fluke. genre-explore-sourced share of the pool: 16.2% (71 of 439), up from a small single-digit share after the first validation batch. eval.js unaffected by design (candidatePool.json isn't read by the eval harness): p10=90/p25=96/p50=98/p100=91, held exactly.
